blockers.whyThisIsABlockerAndNotShouldFix: Two conditions coincide, and either alone would be milder. First, an obligation recorded by an adopted decision against this specific row is orphaned in the very artifact that exists to discharge it — not deferred with a disposition, not routed to an owner, not named as a remainder, simply absent. This corpus's governing discipline on exactly this point is that a deferral 'gets its recorded disposition, never silence'; here there is silence. Second, the artifact's own record of the governing requirement is narrowed so that the orphaning is not visible from the artifact: a coordinator checking this candidate against the requirement as the candidate states it would find the requirement fully met. That is the same failure shape as making an unowned obligation look owned. Unlike defects I have graded SHOULD-FIX elsewhere, there is no correct statement elsewhere in the artifact to fall back on — nothing in it mentions the second obligation at all.

verdictBasis: 1 blocker, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories. The dispatch gate was 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. REJECT.
verdictStatement: The extraction itself is careful and, where it is complete, correct. Thirty-one carried lines across two file 04 sections are byte-exact, the DR-110 row is byte-exact with a uniquely resolving anchor, all three source digests are live at the current HEAD, and the structured rules are faithful to the prose they come from — including a token the source splits across a line break, which the artifact reassembles correctly rather than mangling. It invents no repair medium, transport, format or API; it routes reserved work only to register rows that exist, all six of which I confirmed; and it draws the DR-107/G18 versus self-update rollback boundary cleanly, with a no-silent-reuse rule and independent corroboration in the corpus. Under a forbidden-token audit every SATISFIED and SATISFY is a denial or an imperative. What fails is completeness against the one recorded instruction that governs this artifact's existence. D-002 says the DR-110 disposition, when authored, must draw that rollback boundary AND address file 02's unexercised 'updates' inventory entry. The artifact does the first and is silent on the second — not deferred, not routed, not reserved, not listed among its seven denials; the words 'file 02', 'updates' and 'inventory' do not appear in it at all. And the sentence imposing the requirement is reproduced in the artifact's own recorded inputs only as far as the conjunction, closing with a semicolon at exactly the word where the undone half begins, while the three other properties in that list are recorded whole. So the omission is not merely incomplete work; as recorded, the requirement appears satisfied. This corpus's rule for exactly this situation is that a deferral gets its recorded disposition and never silence, and there is no other statement in the artifact for the gap to resolve against. Beneath that sits a smaller error of the same family: ID-DEP-U3 marks DR-G08 'Not slice-1-required', when D-002 places G08 inside the slice-1 required-gate set scoped to install trust surfaces and defers only its repair-media/rollback surfaces with this row — a distinction the artifact's own sliceStanding draws correctly two keys earlier, naming G06/G11 exactly as D-002 does. Both repairs are available in the source the artifact already cites, in the same D-002 entry, and neither requires a decision this row cannot make.

coordinatorNote: REJECT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-110 stays OPEN at file 08 line 292; I did not touch file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, marked no row SATISFIED (DR-110 and DR-103 included), invented no repair-media API, minted no D-096 (A) grant, and did not commit. Six things to weigh. First, the blocker is about an omission plus how it is recorded, so please read the two together: the missing half of D-002's requirement would be a fair SHOULD-FIX on its own, but the artifact's quotation of that requirement stops at the conjunction, which makes the gap invisible from the artifact — that combination is what moved it. Second, both repairs are small and need no new decision: quote the D-002 sentence to its end, then either address file 02's 'updates' inventory entry here or record it explicitly as an unmet remainder with its standing named. Third, the G08 correction is one clause and D-002 supplies the exact wording — install trust surfaces in slice 1, repair-media/rollback surfaces deferring with this row — which is a sharper statement of the dependency than the one currently written. Fourth, worth flagging beyond this artifact: the 'unexercised updates inventory entry' obligation appears exactly once in the entire repository, in D-002 itself, and nothing has ever addressed it. Whatever happens to this candidate, that item is live and currently unowned in practice; if the coordinator concludes it does not belong to this row, that reassignment is a separate decision and not one I make here. Fifth, everything the artifact does do, it does well — a v2 fixing these two items would, on my measurement, carry zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX. Sixth, the Codex verdict appeared on disk partway through my pass; I measured it at 726b464f… and did not open it, so the lanes are uncorrelated and any convergence on the D-002 completeness point is genuine.
